issues.description: Method signature mismatch for SealSaloon.checkOrderReady. The problem statement (UML and textual instructions) specifies a parameterless method named checkOrderReady(): void that orderMeal() should call. The solution implementation declares public void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) (SealSaloon.java) and orderMeal() calls checkOrderReady(true). This difference in parameter list (no parameter in the spec vs. one boolean in the solution) creates an API inconsistency that will confuse students about the required method signature and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the API consistent between the specification and the reference implementation. Two options:
1) Prefer the specification: change the solution to implement public void checkOrderReady() (no parameters) and update orderMeal() to call checkOrderReady(). If logging or a debug flag is needed in the solution, move it to a private helper or use a class-level flag so the public API matches the spec.
2) Prefer the implementation: update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to declare checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and document the boolean parameter, and adjust examples in the text to show calling checkOrderReady(true/false).
Choose one option and apply it consistently in the UML, textual description, and SealSaloon.java so students have a single, unambiguous required signature.
